display.purpose: Page h1 and homepage hero only. Tight tracking makes it read as a masthead.

body.purpose: All prose, held to --measure (42rem) for 65–75 characters.

label.purpose: Meta lines, nav, kickers, footer. Uppercase and tracked is the system's only decorative move.

code.purpose: Inline code and code blocks, usually on --mark.

breakpoints.name: grid-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: post-card and project-grid both go single-column.

breakpoints.name: figure-scale
breakpoints.purpose: 44rem. Inline SVG figures step their label size from 15px to 24px.

motion.name: scroll-smooth
motion.purpose: The only motion declared. Everything else is a state change with no transition, and prefers-reduced-motion forces it off.

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: The one pill in the system and the only control on every page. Switches light/dark and persists the choice.
components.html: <button class="ds-theme-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Toggle color theme"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" width="16" height="16"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4"></circle><path d="M12 3v2M12 19v2M4.2 4.2l1.4 1.4M18.4 18.4l1.4 1.4M3 12h2M19 12h2M4.2 19.8l1.4-1.4M18.4 5.6l1.4-1.4"></path></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-theme-toggle { width: 2.1rem; height: 2.1rem; border: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--bg-elevated); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 0; } .ds-theme-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Uppercase Outfit chrome. Active and hover go to ink, never to oxblood — nav stays out of the accent's way.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1.35rem; font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 0.86rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-nav a { text-decoration: none; color: var(--muted); } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a.is-active { color: var(--ink); } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Post Card
components.description: An asymmetric 8.5rem meta column beside a fluid body, separated by hairlines top and bottom. Hover moves the h3 colour and nothing else.
components.html:
29 JUNE 2025
6 min

Vibe coding an old blog

Three days with Cursor, a janky Hugo site, and the guidance an AI still needs.
components.css: .ds-post-card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 8.5rem 1fr; gap: 1.6rem; padding: 1.7rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); text-decoration: none; } .ds-post-meta { font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--muted); letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-post-card h3 { font-family: var(--serif-display); font-size: 1.55rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.03em; line-height: 1.2; margin: 0 0 0.45rem; color: var(--ink); } .ds-post-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--ink-soft); font-size: 1.02rem; } .ds-post-card:hover h3 { color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Project Card
components.description: A bordered, raised-paper surface — the only tonal step in the system. Square corners, no shadow.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-project { border: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--bg-elevated); padding: 1.4rem 1.35rem 1.2rem; text-decoration: none; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.45rem; min-height: 11rem; } .ds-project h3 { font-family: var(--serif-display); font-size: 1.35rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.02em; margin: 0; color: var(--ink); } .ds-project p { margin: 0; color: var(--ink-soft); font-size: 0.98rem; flex: 1; } .ds-project .ds-post-meta { font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--muted); letter-spacing: 0.04em; margin-top: 0.4rem; } .ds-project:hover h3 { color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Skip Link
components.description: The only solid oxblood surface in the interface. Parked off-canvas until focused, then it slides in.
components.css: .ds-skip { position: absolute; left: -9999px; top: 0; z-index: 50; background: var(--accent); color: var(--bg); padding: 0.6rem 1rem; font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 0.85rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-decoration: none; } .ds-skip:focus { left: 0; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: IBM Plex Mono on the mark ground, square and full-bleed within the measure. Scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping.
components.css: .ds-code { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.6; background: var(--mark); color: var(--ink); padding: 1.1rem 1.3rem; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0 0 1.4rem; border-radius: 0; } .ds-code code { background: none; padding: 0; font-size: inherit; }

components.name: Blockquote
components.description: A 2px oxblood left rule and italic soft ink. The only place a border is thicker than 1px other than the progress bar.
components.html: If you want an elegant solution, perhaps you need to hold its hand.
components.css: .ds-quote { margin: 1.8rem 0; padding: 0 0 0 1.2rem; border-left: 2px solid var(--accent); color: var(--ink-soft); font-style: italic; } .ds-quote p { margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
A field manual is written to be used, not admired. It is plain, it is durable, and it assumes you will come back to it holding a problem. This system is built the same way: a warm paper ground, a single oxblood ink for anything that matters, hairline rules doing the structural work that other systems delegate to shadows and cards.

The layout is deliberately narrow and columnar. Body text is set at --measure (42rem, roughly 65–75 characters) and the page never exceeds --page (72rem), so the reading experience stays the same whether you arrive on a laptop or a phone. Density is honest: no card corners, no elevation, no ornament that would have to be maintained.

The voice is utilitarian and terse. Headings state what they are, meta lines are uppercase labels rather than prose, and decoration is absent by policy. Warmth comes from exactly two places — the paper tone and the serif — and nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a single oxblood accent; no secondary or tertiary hues
Square corners everywhere, with exactly one pill (the theme toggle)
Structure carried by 1px hairlines, never by shadow
A serif/sans/mono split with one job per face, and one serif doing both display and prose at different weights
Restrained but warm: the material does the personality work, the shapes stay plain

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue. Oxblood appears on well under 10% of any screen; its scarcity is what makes it read as emphasis. A second accent hue is a redesign, not an addition.

rules.name: The Tinted Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never pure black or pure grey. Every ink is tinted toward the ground it sits on — cooled here, because the ground is cool (#14181a, not #000) — so type sits on the page rather than being cut out of it.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Newsreader carries the whole page. Weight and size do the separating — 500 for structural headings, 400 for prose. Reaching for a second serif to manufacture that contrast is the failure this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Uppercase Means Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase plus letter-spacing marks something as metadata, never as content. If a line is meant to be read as a sentence, it does not get tracked caps.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, never cast. If two things need to be told apart, they get a 1px border or a background step — not a shadow, not a glow, not a gradient.

dos: Do hold prose to --measure (42rem) — the reading column is the product.
Do reach for a 1px --hairline when two things need separating.
Do keep oxblood scarce; it is the only emphasis the system has.
Do set interface and meta text in uppercase Outfit with letter-spacing.
Do keep corners square. The theme toggle is the single sanctioned exception.
Do check both themes — every token has a night counterpart, and the accent warms from #8c3b28 to #d08064.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, a gradient, or a glow.
Don't introduce shadows or elevation. Separation is drawn, never cast.
Don't use pure black or pure grey; every ink is warmed toward the paper.
Don't put text on a coloured ground unless it is --paper on --oxblood (the skip link is the only precedent, and it measures 7:1).
Don't set content in tracked uppercase — that treatment means "this is a label".
Don't set body prose above weight 400; weight is how display is separated from reading.
Don't introduce a second serif to create display contrast.
